practices.practice: Create one MongoClient / driver client per process (a singleton) and reuse it across requests rather than creating a new client per request; tune maxPoolSize for expected concurrency.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single, long-lived Motor/Beanie client instance (shared across threads/requests) and avoid creating a new Mongo client per request; configure maxPoolSize to a sensible value (for example 100) rather than leaving an unbounded pool.

practices.practice: Do not commit cluster connection strings or credentials to source control; read DOCUMENTDB_URI and other secrets from environment variables or a secret store (for example, Azure Key Vault) and provide only a .env.example placeholder in the repo.
practices.prior_belief: Never commit the cluster connection string or credentials to source control: read DOCUMENTDB_URI (and any username/password) from environment variables and/or store secrets in Azure Key Vault; provide only a .env.example with placeholders in the repo.

practices.practice: Always connect to Azure DocumentDB with TLS enabled (tls=true) and do not disable certificate validation in production.

practices.practice: Use server-side JSON Schema validation (the MongoDB $jsonSchema validator) where available and also validate/canonicalize inputs in the application; keep the original free-text report in a raw_text field and write parsed typed fields separately.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side schema validation (Beanie/Pydantic before insert and MongoDB schema validation rules where available) and reject or quarantine malformed records; store the original free-text in a raw_text field and the parsed fields as typed fields (drug, event, severity, onset_date as ISODate).

practices.practice: Create a compound index that matches the aggregation/grouping access pattern (for example { drug: 1, event: 1 }) so the GROUP/COUNT aggregation can be satisfied efficiently rather than scanning the collection.
practices.prior_belief: Create a compound index on the fields used by the aggregation (e.g., { drug: 1, event: 1 }) to support GROUP/COUNT aggregations efficiently rather than scanning full collection; create additional index on onset_date if queries filter by date.

practices.practice: For vector similarity search store embeddings in a dedicated top-level field and create an explicit vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF) with parameters (dimensions, similarity metric, maxDegree/lBuild/lSearch) that exactly match your embedding model and query-time similarity.
practices.prior_belief: For vector similarity search, store embedding vectors in a dedicated field (e.g., embedding: [float]) and create a vector index (HNSW/IVF) with explicit parameters (dimension, metric, M/efConstruction or indexType/metric params) tuned to your embedding size; avoid storing vectors in deeply nested fields.

practices.practice: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors and throttling (HTTP 429); when a Retry-After header is present, honor it rather than retrying immediately.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors and 429 throttling responses; on 429, honor Retry-After if provided and back off rather than retrying immediately.
practices.source_name: Design throttling to improve resilience / Retry-After guidance

practices.practice: Rely on the account-level configured consistency (the service maps MongoDB write/read concerns to Cosmos consistency); the default is session-consistency — prefer that rather than trying to emulate strong cross-region consistency in the app.
practices.prior_belief: Use session-level consistency (or the account's configured Cosmos consistency) rather than attempting to emulate strong consistency in the app; avoid expecting immediate cross-region strong consistency for Mongo API unless account configuration guarantees it.

practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB consistency mapping MongoDB API

practices.practice: Prefer single-document atomic operations when possible; avoid multi-document transactions for normal workloads because they increase contention and complexity — keep transactions short and retry on conflict when needed.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid multi-document transactions where possible; design documents so updates are single-document atomic operations (embed related fields in one document) to improve performance and avoid the complexity of distributed transactions.
practices.source_name: Use Multi-document transactions in Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

practices.practice: For large aggregation pipelines use allowDiskUse:true (where supported), and reduce intermediate sizes by filtering/projecting early (match/project/limit early) to avoid memory pressure.
practices.prior_belief: Use allowDiskUse:true for large aggregation pipelines that may exceed memory limits, and project/limit early in the pipeline to reduce intermediate document sizes and memory pressure.

practices.practice: When building or reindexing large indexes, schedule index creation during low-traffic windows and prefer background/index-build-safe approaches; for large data loads, batch inserts rather than single inserts.
practices.prior_belief: When seeding or building large indexes, create indexes offline or during low-traffic windows and prefer background index builds if supported; for very large collections consider batching inserts rather than inserting one-by-one.

practices.practice: Avoid logging or persisting PHI/PII unnecessarily; if you store raw_text for auditing or re-parsing, protect it with least-privilege access, encryption at rest (CMK when needed), and consider field-level encryption.
practices.prior_belief: Don't log or persist raw PHI/PII in plaintext beyond what is necessary; if you must keep raw_text for auditing or re-parsing, protect it with access controls and consider encryption-at-rest and field-level encryption for sensitive fields.

practices.practice: Use a TTL index (expireAfterSeconds on a date field) to implement automated retention/expiry of documents rather than manual delete scripts when appropriate.
practices.prior_belief: Implement document TTL (a TTL index on an expiry field) for retention policies (e.g., automatically expire reports after retention period) rather than manual deletion scripts, to reduce operational overhead.

practices.practice: Enable diagnostics and slow-query logging, collect query performance metrics (explain, keysExamined/docsExamined), and alert on CPU/memory/IOPS/connection saturation for production clusters.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and monitor query performance and usage (OPCOUNTS, slow query logs, or the DocumentDB/MCP profiling tools) and create indexes only after identifying slow aggregation/lookup patterns with explain() plans.

practices.practice: Use bulk/batched writes (insert_many / bulk API) for seeding and high-throughput ingestion rather than single inserts to reduce round-trips and improve throughput; respect service batch/write limits.
practices.prior_belief: Use bulk/batched writes (bulk_insert/insert_many) for seeding and high-throughput ingestion rather than single inserts to reduce round-trips and improve throughput; respect the cluster's RU/throughput limits when batching.
practices.source_name: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB batch write limits insert_many guidance

practices.practice: Protect the DocumentDB endpoint with network controls: use Private Endpoint / VNet integration or firewall rules and avoid exposing clusters to the public internet when possible.
practices.prior_belief: Protect the DocumentDB endpoint with network controls: restrict allowed client IPs, use VNet/private endpoints if available, and avoid exposing the cluster to the public internet without firewall rules.

practices.practice: Treat LLM-driven extraction outputs as untrusted: validate, canonicalize, map to controlled vocabularies, log parse confidence, and quarantine ambiguous results rather than writing them directly to production structured fields.
practices.prior_belief: When using LLM-driven extraction, treat the LLM output as untrusted: validate and canonicalize fields (normalize drug names, map severities to controlled vocabulary) and log parse confidence; quarantine ambiguous parses rather than writing invalid structured data.

practices.practice: Test durability/writeConcern behavior on the Mongo API because writeConcern/readConcern options are mapped to the account's configured consistency and some Mongo writeConcern behaviors may be limited or differ under the service compatibility layer.
practices.prior_belief: Use appropriate writeConcern or durability settings for critical writes (e.g., w=majority) when available, but test behavior on the Cosmos Mongo API because some Mongo writeConcern options may be limited or behave differently under the Cosmos MongoDB compatibility layer.
